deep_competitors.offering: Complete AI-native sales platform: AI-native CRM (custom objects, auto-updates, 'Ask Reevo' AI assistant), prospecting + enrichment (Find), sales engagement + dialer (Connect), meeting intelligence + deal management (Sell), and forecasting + coaching (Manage). One platform intended to replace Salesforce/HubSpot + Outreach/Salesloft + ZoomInfo + Gong + Clari. Built by ex-DoorDash engineering leadership.
deep_competitors.ai_talk: Confident, outcome-focused, and anti-Frankenstack. The core narrative: 'A CRM nobody updates. A call recorder. An outbound tool. Each one sees a fragment, so the AI bolted onto them is guessing.' Positions Reevo as the only AI that 'actually knows' because it has full context from every deal. Talks about AI that 'compounds' rather than assists. Tone: pragmatic, engineering-credible, no fluff. Customer quote: 'Coming from HubSpot, Reevo was truly a breath of fresh air.'
deep_competitors.integrations: Email: Gmail, Outlook (managed deliverability, domain purchase built-in). Calendar: Google, Outlook. CRM: built-in AI-native CRM + Salesforce/HubSpot sync (via integrations). Dialer: built-in click-to-call. Voice: built-in meeting recording. Slack: native (Ask Reevo in any channel). MCP connectors (new as of Oct 2026 — pulls context from external tools into Ask Reevo). SOC2 implied (not explicitly confirmed on site).

g2_1star.quote: Very new product — 10 G2 reviews total as of Nov 2026, all skewing positive. No significant negative review patterns available publicly. Given Series A stage (Nov 2025) and early customer base, critical feedback is limited.

Intent signals and signal prospecting (key competitive features vs ZoomInfo/Apollo) are listed as 'Soon' on the pricing comparison — not yet shipped, which could be a gap for prospects needing those capabilities now.

deep_competitors.monday_angle: Reevo is the most direct structural competitor to monday.com's sales CRM vision — both are building unified platforms to replace the Frankenstack, with AI at the core. Reevo has a head start on AI-native CRM architecture, deal intelligence, and outbound, but lacks monday.com's brand, existing user base, and PM integrations.
deep_competitors.other_insights: Founded April 2024. Founders all have DoorDash backgrounds: David Zhu (CEO — ex-Head of Engineering at DoorDash, scaled from $700M to $75B market cap at IPO), Cindy Hao (Co-Founder — ex-Atomic/OpenStore), Clement Fang (Co-Founder — ex-DoorDash platform engineering), Curtis [Anh] (Co-Founder, also ex-DoorDash). This is an execution-credibility founding team: they built at massive scale before. $80M raised from Khosla Ventures + Kleiner Perkins — top-tier VCs signal conviction in the category. Valuation ~$500M. Blog strategy is aggressively SEO-focused (comparison articles vs HubSpot, Salesforce, ZoomInfo, etc.) to capture bottom-of-funnel traffic from competitors' existing users. SaaStr Annual 2026 talk: 'How Reevo Hit Its Number With Half the Reps' — signals they're proving unit economics with existing customers. GTMnow podcast 'Inside Reevo's $80M Bet to Kill the $10B Frankenstein Stack' is the best overview of their thesis.

deep_competitors.value_prop: Work management platform for enterprise teams — not a CRM, but positions two sales plays: (1) Smartsheet CRM via configurable templates, (2) Smartsheet for Sales teams (pipeline tracking, territory management, deal reviews as structured grids + automation).

deep_competitors.icp: Enterprise (1,000+ employees); cross-functional teams (PMO, ops, sales ops, marketing). NOT typical sales reps — buyers are IT/ops/PMO.
deep_competitors.persona: VP Operations, PMO Director, Sales Ops Manager, RevOps. NOT AEs or SDRs primarily.
deep_competitors.pricing_tiers: Pro $9/member/mo · Business $19/member/mo · Enterprise custom · Advanced Work Management custom (all billed annually)

deep_competitors.offering: Horizontal work management platform (not a CRM). Two sales-relevant plays: 1) Smartsheet CRM — template-based lead/account/contact management. 2) Smartsheet for Sales — pipeline views, territory management, deal review boards, quota tracking — all as configurable Smartsheet grids with automation.
deep_competitors.ai_talk: Tone: enterprise-responsible. Key claims: 'AI that learns your pace, patterns, risks.' Anti-positioning: 'Most AI tools treat every session as a blank slate — Smartsheet AI doesn't.' Trust messaging: permissions-aware agents, works within existing governance. No claim of autonomous SDR or CRM replacement.
deep_competitors.integrations: Salesforce, HubSpot, Jira, Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, Slack, Teams; Zapier; MCP to Claude/Copilot/Gemini/ChatGPT/Amazon Q
deep_competitors.monday_angle: Directly comparable in horizontal work management + AI agents narrative. Smartsheet targets enterprise PMO/ops buyers; monday AI Workspace targets both ops and sales teams directly. Smartsheet's MCP play is a credible threat — same narrative (bring AI to your existing tools) but deeper enterprise integration story.
deep_competitors.other_insights: Acquired by Blackstone in 2024 for ~$8.4B. Despite going private, retained NYSE listing and is functionally public-company grade. ENGAGE 2026 launched vsActual and AI agents — signals full AI platform pivot, not just features. No dedicated AI SDR or autonomous prospecting play — biggest gap vs. 11x/Artisan/Reevo.

light_check.name: Asana
light_check.summary: Asana has broad horizontal AI ('Agentic Work Management') with 30+ prebuilt AI Teammates across marketing, IT, operations, manufacturing, retail, and healthcare — but no sales-specific AI agents or CRM functionality. There is no dedicated sales offering; sales teams would use Asana for project tracking, not pipeline management or prospecting. Asana's 'Dash' AI (chief-of-staff routing) and 'AI Studio' (no-code automations) are general-purpose workflow tools, not sales-native.

light_check.name: ClickUp
light_check.summary: ClickUp has a dedicated Sales Teams page with 'Super Agents' specifically scoped to sales workflows: Pipeline Agent, Forecast Agent, Enablement Agent, Prep Agent, Stakeholder Agent, Renewal Agent, QBR Agent, and Expansion Agent. This is more than templates — it's purpose-built AI for deal management. However, ClickUp is still fundamentally a project/work management platform (not a CRM or outbound tool), and these agents operate on tasks/records within ClickUp rather than integrating natively with CRM or email outbound sequences. No AI SDR, no prospecting, no call intelligence.

light_check.name: Notion
light_check.summary: Notion's CRM presence is entirely template-based (2,224+ CRM templates in its gallery). There is no dedicated sales AI — Notion AI is general-purpose (writing, summarizing, Q&A within pages). No pipeline management, no outbound AI, no deal intelligence. Notion redirects sales CRM queries to its template gallery, confirming no native sales product. The 'use-case/crm' URL redirects to the template category.

light_check.name: Airtable
light_check.summary: Airtable has a dedicated Sales CRM solution page with real AI features: AI-generated account plans, buying committee mapping, expansion opportunity surfacing (predicting upsell/cross-sell/renewal risk), and pipeline visibility. It also integrates with Salesforce, HubSpot, and Gong. However, Airtable is a flexible database platform (not a native CRM) — it positions itself as 'the operational layer that extends CRM capabilities' alongside existing tools, not a replacement. There is no AI SDR, no outbound sequencing, and no meeting intelligence.
